title: fix: recover managed Gateways after updates and repairs
body:
Closes #157205
Closes #157227
Closes #147357

## What Problem This Solves

Updates and repairs could reject a stopped systemd unit as an ownership change and leave the Gateway down; standalone Doctor could finish repairing an already-stopped Gateway without starting it.

## User Impact

Managed Gateways can recover after failed updates and repairs, including restarting the previous installation after rollback. Git-to-npm updates refresh the service to use the new installation. Successful standalone `doctor --fix` also starts and verifies an already-stopped, owned Gateway targeting the current installation.

Ownership, current-authority, installation-drift, and data-safety checks remain enforced. Update-time Doctor leaves activation with its updater.

## Why This Change Was Made

systemd can collect an inactive unit while its installed definition remains intact. Requiring an already-loaded command then failed before the updater could refresh the launcher or recover the previous service. The update service-inspection owner now uses its retained manager identity and current native/caller authority to reload unit metadata. Restart preparation, failure recovery, and rollback share that operation. Doctor reuses its existing restoration and readiness owner for a successfully repaired, previously stopped service.

The three expensive legacy-driver cases now use the existing opt-in live tier, collected by `vitest.live.config.ts` and `pnpm test:all`. Their shared assertions are preserved; the remaining 14 cases run in ordinary PR CI. No new test tier or configuration was introduced.

Thanks @Matuno, @DonnieFi, and @Navras98 for the reports.

## Evidence

- Inherited failure: `test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts` still searches the parent Bun script for `assert-release-versions` after #159439 moved it into `ai-candidate.sh`; main hourly 23:29Z is red, and the main fix is being handled separately.
- Pre-fix controls: the three collected-unit regression cases failed without the production patch; the registered Doctor flow performed repair without restart. Candidate controls pass. Published 2026.9.5 also reproduced successful Doctor exit with the owned unit still inactive; the candidate starts it and verifies readiness.
- After rebasing, 129 importer files passed: 5,357 tests across 11 Vitest shards. Touched suites and the three legacy-driver live cases passed three times. [Importer/repetition run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36312200306), lease `tbx_01m3h629kk0gt58ma1a91vtr5t`; the remote batch exited 0 in 43m52s. Four helper-registered suites completed their third run separately: [helper-suite run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36315168951), lease `tbx_01m3h986hp632w156vj32cny3c`.
- Latest `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed, including core/test/script typechecks, lint, dead exports, and guards. [Final check run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36312199486), lease `tbx_01m3h628mggyktvtspy6df0bc6`; final command exited 0 in 22m49s. The linked runs identify Testbox leases; command exit codes establish the proof result.
- Fresh isolated Codex autoreview at P1: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Real Linux systemd user-service proof used isolated profiles and free ports:

| Flow | Observed terminal result |
| --- | --- |
| Standalone Doctor on an owned stopped Gateway | New running PID; readiness true |
| Repair deadline after the real pending-plugin warning | Doctor child settled; previous Gateway restarted and ready |
| Unmodified published 2026.9.5 updater; staged Doctor read stall after the real pending-plugin warning | `doctor-failed`; original package hashes and running PID preserved; readiness true |
| Published 2026.9.5 → candidate | `succeeded`; new package serving; readiness true |
| Candidate native serving process exits 78 after passing canary | Previous package restored; selected package hashes matched; Gateway restarted and ready |
| Git-linked checkout → npm stable | Service `ExecStart` and live PID target the new npm installation; channel persisted as stable; readiness true |

[Complete rebased live matrix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36312199296), lease `tbx_01m3h628bhvj40km01an7ynag8`; package preparation and all service cells exited 0 in 21m31s. Rollback verified exact prior serving-launcher, package manifest, build identity, and runtime-inventory hashes. Detached update handoffs were joined through their recorded terminal outcome and settled driver identities.

The pending-plugin proof uses a synthetic installed plugin exercising the actual install-record deferral contract, with one injected Doctor read stall. The activation fault is restricted to the native serving command. These prove service availability; they do not claim completion of Google Chat-specific data migration.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and change size</summary>

The combined 17-case refusal file previously took 125.908 / 132.830 / 127.703 seconds of test time. After separating the existing live contracts:

| Tier | Test time, three runs | File wall time, three runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PR CI, 14 cases | 60.727 / 57.150 / 55.203s | 76.32 / 71.42 / 68.86s |
| Existing live tier, 3 cases | 76.501 / 71.023 / 67.749s | 95.41 / 88.69 / 84.62s |

The table records isolated one-worker runs through the repository test wrapper. The rebased validation repeated the split suites; its live-case test totals were 73.839 / 69.368 / 68.815s (94.41 / 86.79 / 87.64s file wall). Shared compiler/runtime preparation is separate. The change also removes a duplicate 31-second delayed probe, checks the caller's actual timeout budget at the runner boundary, and shares read-only inspection workers for the original-service fixture. No retries, weakened assertions, or increased timeouts were introduced.

The additional CI-planner importers exercise complete repository plans; their slowest observed case was 85.211s. Those suites already belong to the existing release-only tooling tier and passed unchanged.

Production: +55/−21 (net +34), reduced from +52 by centralizing repeated missing-manager checks and combining a redundant diagnostic-string concatenation without changing its text. Test routing: +6/−1. Tests/support: +606/−405, including the moved legacy-driver matrix. Docs: +12/−7.

</details>
